text:
incident-bot: PAGER P1 - GPU OOM spike on decode-shard-12 (streaming). Auto-escalation enabled. Symptoms: node flaps, request drops, 500s to customer traffic. Runbook: https://redwood.incidents/1769009999 — please ack :pager:

maya: acked. seeing OOMs across multiple decode nodes, started around 11:58 UTC. request drops on streaming path, approx 8k errors in 10m window.

pranav: i'm oncall, taking ownership. first actions: quarantine bad nodes, reduce batch_size on decode pool, enforce temporary per-request token cap, and route traffic to fallback smaller model. will post commands.

kevin: which model and quantization variant? any recent rollout?

infra-bot: Telemetry snapshot:
- affected_pool: decode-shard-12
- model: redwood-v2-decoder-13b-quant
- error: cudaErrorIllegalAddress / cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
- start: 2026-03-15T11:58:42Z
- approx failures: 8220 requests (last 10m)

maya: no deliberate rollout in last 24h. kernel/driver updates?

pranav: running quick health checks. stepping through mitigations now.

pranav: Mitigation plan (executing):
1) mark decode-shard-12 pool as quarantine (stop new allocations)
2) patch runtime config: clamp max_tokens_per_request to 2000 for streaming endpoints
3) reduce continuous batching target from 8 -> 4 to lower peak allocs
4) route 30% traffic to redwood-v2-decoder-6b as fallback for streaming
5) spin up fresh nodes with same kernel and warm KV cache

pranav: running commands:
```
# quarantine pool
rbctl pools update decode-shard-12 --drain --no-new-allocs
# lower batch size
rbctl config set serving.decode.batch_target 4
# apply temporary token clamp on streaming route
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://api.redwood.internal/configs/streams -d '{"max_tokens_per_request":2000}'
```

support-bot: Customer impact: ticket T-12345 (Searchify) reported streaming failures at 11:59 UTC. Enterprise customer S-668 reporting 40% request failures on streaming generate. Internal estimate: multi-tenant hosted customers saw ~6% error rate overall during spike.

anya: adding header-based clamp as rapid guard: if X-Requested-Tokens > 3000 then reject with 400+ explanatory body. pushing policy now.

pranav: applied clamp, reduced batch target, and started traffic shift to 6b fallback. monitoring for OOMs.

infra-bot: Logs from a failing container (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-15T11:59:03Z] ERR decode_loop.cpp:462 cudaErrorIllegalAddress at 0x7f8b1a2d4000
[2026-03-15T11:59:03Z] WARN Allocating 8192MB for KV cache growth
[2026-03-15T11:59:03Z] INFO free mem before alloc: 512MB
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
```

kevin: looks like KV cache growth + long-running streaming sessions pushed the allocation over threshold. any long prefixes?

maya: telemetry shows a tail of very long sessions (some clients had max_tokens unset / header bypass) — we've seen header-bypass variants slip through earlier filters.

pranav: adding quick fix to enforce prefix cache expiry and hard per-session token cap on runtime. will follow up with a hotpatch to the runtime to evict prefix cache faster.

sara: spun up 4 replacement nodes in eu-west-1 and warmed KV cache from snapshots. new nodes are healthy and serving fallback.

pranav: Current status update (t+30m):
- quarantine in place, no new allocations to decode-shard-12
- batch target reduced across streaming pools
- header-based clamp and token cap applied
- 30% traffic routed to 6b fallback; failing request rate down from 40% -> 6% for impacted customers
- customer-facing incidents page drafted, support notified customers in impacted list

support-bot: Drafted external blurb for Searchify and S-668. ETA to send: 20m after triage signoff.

kevin: root-cause hypothesis: runaway generation from misconfigured max_tokens + KV cache growth on decode-13b-quant -> OOM on CUDA allocation path. Need full trace and mem accounting to confirm.

maya: agree. also add telemetry check to detect header bypass variants (X-Max-Tokens > 10000 or missing).

pranav: action items assigned:
- pranaV: follow up runtime hotpatch to evict prefix cache faster (PR #4381), coordinate rollback if hotpatch destabilizes
- maya: collect full heap traces, OOM timelines, and sample failing request headers/logs
- kevin: run replay on staging with long-session traces to reproduce KV growth
- support: customer comms and ticket correlation (map accounts to affected orgs)

anya: open question: do we want an automatic per-customer token quota at the router level? seems useful to prevent future multi-tenant blasts.

sara: agreed, but that is product work. short-term: enforce runtime clamps and better monitoring.

pranav: preparing incident bridge notes for handoff to night oncall at 18:00 UTC. will include mitigation timeline, affected customers, and next steps.

incident-bot: P1 acknowledged by pranav at 1769009999. Incident remains P1. Next update expected in 20m. :fire:

maya: small follow-up — observed one container crash loop on node decode-12-03, we captured core dump and driver logs. saving to /artifacts/1769009999/ for postmortem.

kevin: thanks everyone. once stable, let's run an eval to ensure quality delta for 6b fallback acceptable for affected routes.

support-bot: closing note: Escalated account execs for S-668 and Searchify, preparing interim credit offers. will include timeline in follow-up.

pranav: will leave the thread open until we complete handoff and postmortem skeleton.

sara: noted. handing to night oncall @dmitri in bridge. attaching bridge link: https://meet.redwood/incident-1769009999

incident-bot: update recorded. last action at 1769013600."
